follow-on: _reage_budget_report returns the stored report object unchanged when the interval since built_at is zero, so the dict handed back on a same-moment call is the cached entry itself; a caller that mutates any field of the result mutates the cache. A deep copy on the zero-delta path (cache_root is the caller's, but the picker's own callers are not all read-only) closes it.

follow-on: the declared negative control ran 4 tests (...F) rather than the six-case file it belongs to; the control is on-point (neutralizing the age recompute reddens test_advancing_the_clock_changes_ages_but_not_file_derived_fields, EXIT=1), but running the whole file would also prove the two attribution cases stay green under the mutation.

justifications.durability: the cache-hit assertions are read of live objects rather than test-supplied constants: the second-call test monkeypatches snapshot.budget.preflight and builtins.open and asserts the paid-lanes document is not reopened, so a revert of the cache reddens it, and the touch test rewrites the document and asserts the preflight count rises; but the negative control as logged ran a 4-test subset (...F) rather than the six-case file, and _reage_budget_report returns the stored report object by reference when the interval is zero, so a caller mutating a same-moment result mutates the cached entry.
justifications.evidence: logs/gate_base.log and logs/gate_head.log record base 186 passed EXIT=0 and head 192 passed EXIT=0, a delta of +6 equal to the added file's size, and the reviewed negative control is on-point (neutralizing the age recompute in _reage_budget_report reddens the age test, EXIT=1, 1 failed/3 passed); I independently re-ran the reviewed tests/test_budget_view_is_cached.py against the head tree (6 passed, EXIT=0). It does not reach a top score: the cost figure the brief cites (286 ms) is not reconciled with the recorded before median of 10839 ms, and the evidence fragment states the warm maximum as 1.3 ms while after.json records read_counts [2749, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6] with max_ms 829.6 ms - the cold build - so the max is reported without its cold first sample.
justifications.fit: the cache reuses the existing capabilities.cached_pick_input_stamped idiom (root= cache_root) that routing.context_census and routing._estimated_hours already call, and the new symbols _budget_view_input_paths, _budget_view_request_key, _compose_budget_report, _reage_budget_report are named by mechanism with no plan, ticket or version id; the pre-existing cached_only backend override moves into the wrapper unchanged at snapshot.py:614-622.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the file-derived report is cached on the stamps of every file the view reads (paid-lanes document, banked-reset record, per-backend lane documents, and the ledger index via ledger.index_stamp, reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:596-602), and every time-derived field is recomputed per call by delta from built_at in _reage_budget_report (:527-570), which returns the stored report unchanged only when the interval is zero; the measured cost falls from median 10839 ms to 1.2 ms warm with the read count falling 2745 to 6, so the goal in full is met.
justifications.reuse: the change introduces no second cache: it routes through the same stamped pick-input cache, and reuses capabilities.file_stamp, ledger.index_stamp, budget.policy and budget.summary rather than reimplementing any of them; _compose_budget_report is the former budget_view body extracted verbatim, so the uncached fallback is the same code path the caller had before.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 7c882130d..76997333f lists only reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, tests/test_budget_view_is_cached.py and docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/budget-view-is-cached.html, all inside the declared write paths; the brief's hold on reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/cli.py is respected - neither appears in the diff.
